demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: Calls from the shell impersonate documind-ui-sa, the UI's own account, which make roster put on the three golden tenants (acme, zeta, globex). That is why a shell call can name any of the three. otok mints a token for documind-outsider-sa, an account IAM admits into the service and no roster lists. Tokens last about an hour; the functions mint a fresh one on every call. Your browser session is different: IAP signs you in as yourself, and the roster maps your email to exactly one tenant. Keep the two apart in your head; step 3 makes the difference visible. The shell, in the kit's folder, with PROJECT, REGION, NUMBER and tok. The peer and the chat must run this lesson's kit: the peer's image with its cap, and the chat's with peer.py and a2a-sdk. If the peer's /health in step 5 names no max_llm_calls, or the chat was deployed before your last git pull, build and deploy them again with this cell. Otherwise skip it.

demos.heading: Why it is built this way, what it costs, and what the kit does not do yet
demos.purpose: Every guard above sits on the lane. One more loop needs neither a hand-off nor a second service: two agents that may each hand the turn to the other, where neither owns the answer. In ADK it is one setting away. An agent under a parent is offered transfer_to_agent, whose agent_name is an enum of the agents it may reach: its parent, and its peers unless disallow_transfer_to_peers is set. commands/agent_shapes.py builds two such desks under a root, scripts each to want the other desk to answer, and puts one plugin on the run, TransferCap. It counts the agents a turn starts in a temp: key, which ADK keeps for one turn and never stores, and once 3 transfers have been made it answers in place of the next agent, before that agent's model is called. Run it offline, at Rs 0. It runs the same turn twice, with the peer edges and without them:

Q: What notice period does a confirmed E3 employee at ACME serve?

== transfers between the desks allowed (ADK's default)
who each agent may transfer to (transfer_to_agent's enum, as its model was offered it):
  desk_root      handbook_desk, statute_desk

transfer 4: handbook_desk -> statute_desk   refused: TransferCap answered before statute_desk ran
